topics.label: Introduction and lecture aims
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning objectives regarding cancer causation, carcinogenicity methodologies, and initiators versus promoters.

topics.label: Cancer causation: endogenous mutations, environmental exposures, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of cancer etiology by examining the balance between endogenous 'bad luck' mutations, inherited genetic predispositions, and environmental risk factors illustrated through global epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens and oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological agents such as viruses, bacteria, and parasites contribute to malignancy, focusing on the mechanism and discovery of Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and xenobiotic metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical agents and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic conversion to form bulky DNA adducts and induce specific mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and host tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, including the initiator-promoter paradigm, inflammation-driven growth, and stage-of-life tissue vulnerability.

topics.label: Methods for determining carcinogenicity and assessing risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the scientific approaches used to identify and validate carcinogens—including mutational signatures, epidemiological biobanks, animal models, and in vitro assays—alongside considerations of dose and risk-benefit balance.
